newsitem.title: UK: Some Euro oil refiners cut runs as margins suffer.
newsitem.headline: Some Euro oil refiners cut runs as margins suffer.

text.p: Some European oil refiners have cut production and others are considering following suit because of poor returns on sales in a weakening late winter heating oil market, oil traders said on Tuesday.
Other refiners, however, say they are still making money and that the market looks too volatile to gamble on a change in production level.
"The market has got to be terrible for much longer to enable us to cut," a trader at a British refiner said.
"The picture is so volatile that it is not clear where we stand," another trader said.

Most oil companies declined to comment publicly but traders said they estimated well over 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude throughput was being taken out of European volumes throughout Feburary, which is roughly equivalent to five standard North Sea cargoes of crude.
European refinery capacity currently stands at 12.6 million bpd.

French major Total is cutting crude intake at its 211,000 bpd Gonfreville refinery near Dunkirk by 100,000 barrels for the month and by 10-15 percent at its 127,000 bpd La Mede plant in southern France, traders said.
British Petroleum said margins were very poor in January and confirmed market talk it was considering cutting runs.

"Our refining margins in January were very disappointing. Decisions are being taken decentrally but it's not surprising that some business managers are considering cuts," said BP Oil chief executive Rolf Stomberg.
Evidence of sliding margins was seen in the collapse in the spread between the price on the physical market for heating oil and international benchmark spot Brent crude in northwest Europe.
Heating oil, also known as gas oil, is the leading oil product in winter when demand peaks, but usually weakens in the spring.
Gas oil's premium to Brent fell from $6.30 a barrel on January 3 to $2.68 on February 6.

"Gas oil is the part of the barrel which should carry the best premium now but the crack (spread) is bad. Gasoline has not taken off yet which it does early in the year as a rule," said a trader at a Northern European refinery.
Crude throughput has been reduced by about 10 percent at the Gothenburg and Lysekil refineries in Sweden, he added.
Irish National Petroleum Corp (INPC) cut throughput at its Whitegate refinery by 30 percent in early February and may drop it further, trading sources said.
Whitegate's minimum throughput is about 50 percent of the 60,000-65,000 barrel per day capacity, trading sources said.
Spanish refinery Petronor declined to comment on talk that it was cutting, but trading sources estimated its 220,000 bpd refinery in Bilbao was currently running under 200,000 bpd.
Italy's ISAB decided on January 31 to cut crude throughput at its 220,000 barrels per day (bpd) Melilli refinery in Sicily, traders said.
Traders familiar with the refinery's operations said the cut, which amounted to a reduction in crude throughput of 10-20 percent, was under constant review.
Elf refinery spokesmen declined to comment on market talk they had taken advantage of the weakening margins to bring forward regular spring maintenance.
